{{DISPLAYTITLE:List of ''Canna'' cultivars}}
This '''list of ''Canna'' cultivars''' is a gallery of named [[cultivar]]s of [[plant]]s in the [[genus]] ''[[Canna (plant)|Canna]]'' that are representative of the various ''Canna'' cultivar groups (i.e., groups of very similar cultivars<ref name="ICNCP" />).

Names of cultivars conform to the rules of the [[International Society for Horticultural Science]] (ISHS) Commission for Nomenclature and Cultivar Registration, as laid down in the [[International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants]]. They are registered with an [[International Cultivar Registration Authority]] (ICRA), which for the genus ''Canna'' is the [[Koninklijke Algemeene Vereniging voor Bloembollencultuur|Royal General Bulbgrowers' Association]] of the Netherlands (KAVB).<ref name="ICNCP">{{cite book
|title = International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants
|first = Christopher D.
|last = Brickell
|publisher = Lubrecht & Cramer Ltd.
|edition = 7th
|date = January 2004
|isbn = 90-6605-527-8}}</ref>

== Foliage group ==
Cultivars, F1 and F2 hybrids, normally with small species-like flowers, but grown principally for their foliage.<ref name="groups">{{cite web
|url = https://cannanews.blogspot.com/2007/04/canna-cultivar-groups.html
|title = Canna cultivar groups
|last = Dalebö
|first = Malcolm
|work = Canna News
|date = April 24, 2007
|accessdate = 2011-05-27}}</ref><ref name="khoshoo">{{cite journal
|last1 = Khoshoo
|first1 = T.N.
|last2 = Guha
|first2 = I.
|title = Origin and Evolution of Cultivated Cannas
|publisher = Vikas Publishing House
|year = 1976
|location = [[New Delhi]]}}</ref><ref name="sid">{{cite book
|title = An Amateur in an Indian Garden
|last = Percy-Lancaster
|first = Sydney
|year = 1927}}</ref> This group has occasionally been referred to as the Année Group, after the originator, [[Théodore Année]], the world's first ''Canna'' hybridizer. However, the use of an accented character in the name creates problems, both in pronunciation and keyboard entry, that it was felt that as they were grown primarily for foliage, then "Foliage Group" was the better name choice.<ref name="groups" />

== Crozy group ==
A cultivar group where the flower spikes are arranged close together on the stalk and have narrow to medium petals. There is always space between the [[staminode]]s when arranged formally,{{clarify|date=June 2012}} and the [[Labellum (botany)|labellum]] (lip) is smaller than the staminodes, and is often twisted or curled.<ref name="groups" /><ref name="khoshoo" /><ref name="sid" /><ref name="compare">{{cite web
|url = https://cannanews.blogspot.com/2007/04/comparison-of-crozy-and-italian-groups.html
|title = Comparison of Crozy and Italian Groups
|last = Dalebö
|first = Malcolm
|work = Canna News
|date = 24 April 2007
|accessdate = 2011-05-27}}</ref>

The pioneer of this group was Monsieur [[Pierre-Antoine-Marie Crozy|Crozy]] of [[Lyon]], France, who started breeding cannas as early as 1862, from stock originally developed by Théodore Année.<ref name="khoshoo" /><ref name="sid" /><ref>{{cite book
|title = Le Canna, son histoire, sa culture
|last = Chaté
|first = E.
|year = 1867
|publisher = Librairie Centrale d'Agriculture et de Jardinage
|language = French}}</ref>

They are sometimes referred to as gladiolus flowering cannas, but describing flowers as similar to another genus is not encouraged.<ref name="cooke">{{cite book
|last = Cooke
|first = Ian
|date = September 1, 2001
|title = The Gardener's Guide to Growing Canna
|publisher = [[Workman Publishing Company|Timber Press]]
|isbn = 978-0-88192-513-5}}</ref> In the past, they were called the ''Canna'' × ''generalis'' [[Liberty Hyde Bailey|L.H. Bailey]] garden species, but the use of [[Grex (horticulture)#Linnean treatment of natural hybrids: the nothospecies|nothospecies]] for complex garden hybrids have been replaced by Cultivar Groups in the [[International Code of Nomenclature for Cultivated Plants]].<ref name="ICNCP" />

== Italian group ==
A cultivar group with large, fragile staminodes.  Flowers are arranged somewhat loosely, with wide petals, so wide that there is no space between them, when arranged formally.  The labellum (lip) is larger, or at least as large, as the staminodes, unlike the other groups where it is smaller and sometimes curled.  The stamen is also much wider than that in the other cultivar groups.<ref name="groups" /><ref name="khoshoo" /><ref name="sid" /><ref name="compare" />

Also, used to be called the orchid flowering cannas, or ''C.'' × ''orchiodes'' [[Liberty Hyde Bailey|L.H. Bailey]] garden species,<ref name="khoshoo" /><ref name="sid" /><ref name="cooke" /> although such "pretend" species are now deprecated in favour of [[Cultivar Group]]s.<ref name="ICNCP" /> In any event, it is difficult to see the similarity between this group and orchids.<ref name="cooke" />

Most of this group obtained its larger sized flowers from the introduction of ''Canna flaccida'' in the early 1890s by [[Carl Ludwig Sprenger|Dr Sprenger]] in Naples, Italy followed shortly afterwards by [[Luther Burbank]] in California, United States, with the same cross.<ref name="khoshoo" /><ref name="sid" />

== Conservatory group ==
The growing conditions in a [[Conservatory (greenhouse)|conservatory]] are quite specialised and do not suit many cultivars, this group have been selected for thriving in this environment, required features being plant vigor, early flowering, foliar appearance, self-cleaning ability and good propagation qualities. The originator of this group was Robert Armstrong (geneticist) while he was working at [[Longwood Gardens]] in the United States in 1967.<ref name="armstrong">{{cite web
|url = http://66.155.36.102/Plants&Horticulture/PlantIntroduction/Armstrong/PlantIntroductionHistory.htm
|title = Plant Introductions
|first = Robert
|last = Armstrong]
}}{{dead link|date=March 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>{{Full citation needed|date=May 2011}}

== Aquatic group ==
Cultivars that thrive as marginal water plants. Characteristically, they will have lance-shaped foliage and long, thin rhizomes.<ref name="groups" /><ref name="khoshoo" /><ref name="sid" /><ref name="cooke" /><ref name="armstrong" />{{Full citation needed|date=May 2011}}

== Musaefolia Group ==
The Musaefolia Group, having large leaves and being either tall or giant in size consists of cultivars whose leaves resemble those of banana plants (genus ''[[Musa (genus)|Musa]]''). Until this group was designated, the cultivars were considered to be members of the Foliage Group.
